revisions.title: Six captures, one elusive sophist
revisions.body: Across six captures, the Stranger repeatedly redirects the same quarry: first the paid hunter of wealthy and promising youths; then the merchant who imports learning, the retailer who sells it locally, and the producer who makes it; then the paid disputant; finally the purifier who strips away false wisdom. The count matters: each route changes the sophist’s apparent art without yet giving us a single stable portrait.

revisions.title: Appearance from the wrong vantage
revisions.body: I take the visual example to turn on an unfavorable viewing position—not a favorable distance: a large work can appear like the beautiful from where it is seen, yet fail to resemble it to someone able to see it adequately. I take that contrast to open the split between likeness and appearance, while leaving the sophist’s placement unsettled.

revisions.title: When denial borrows its terms
revisions.body: I hear this passage less as a doctrine about nothingness than as a demonstration of how quickly language creates commitments. When the Stranger tries to deny unity, plurality, and being to “not-being,” those terms seem to return in the very act of naming. The productive tension, as I read it, is that the hunt is stalled not by a solved definition, but by a vocabulary that has exposed its own difficulty.

revisions.title: A New Defense, Not the Last
revisions.body: My reading is that this is a new defense, not the sophist’s final hiding place. The Stranger’s conditional plan makes the dramatic posture provisional: the inquiry may hold him here, or release him and search in another class. I take the account of speech, opinion, and fancy to open a middle ground for examining seeming without collapsing it into either sheer nothing or truth.

The useful question here is not whether imitation succeeds; I hear the passage granting that it can. The distinction is between two sources of imitation: knowledge and opinion. Keep that distinction in view as the Stranger turns to inspect the opinion-imitator for an internal seam. Can apparent confidence conceal a further division within the imitator himself?
